findings.finding: No authoritative MC-19 Master Prompt is recorded in the repository or supplied in this milestone mandate.
findings.evidence: MASTER-PROMPT-REGISTRY header: prompts 03-36 are planning placeholders; the client-issued Master Prompt is authoritative. No MC-19 Master Prompt is recorded. Repository absence cannot prove non-issuance: MC-18 records that its own authorising prompt existed but was never committed while registry row 18 still said PLANNED (MC-18-BASELINE-AND-GOVERNANCE.md section 3). P01 is asserted from the mandate and the absence of a recorded approval, not from the placeholder alone.
findings.impact: Implementation would lack a recorded contractual scope; the stop decision also rests on independently verifiable blockers.

findings.finding: The owners segment has no MC-15 proposed route, entity or page type.
findings.evidence: proposed-routes.json contains professionals and installers, but no owners/armadores route. Handoff section 6 calls an owner page 'possible'.
findings.impact: A new IA decision is required before an owner page can exist.

findings.finding: Every enquiry/lead flow is blocked by an open privacy gate.
findings.evidence: GATE-PRIVACY-DPA-DPIA is BLOCKED; 24 required documents, 0 executed; handoff section 9 lists six prerequisites.
findings.impact: The 'lead flows' part of the MC-19 expected output cannot be implemented or tested now.

findings.finding: Publication, indexation and deployment are not authorized.
findings.evidence: D23 records publication NOT_AUTHORIZED, merge/deploy/publish false; no release authorization record exists.
findings.impact: MC-19 pages must remain isolated internal previews if later approved.

findings.finding: The MC-19 acceptance criterion is a theme, not a measurable contract.
findings.evidence: Registry row 19 verification column: 'Real CTAs only (quote/pre-registration/coming-soon per readiness)'.
findings.impact: Acceptance criteria must be proposed and approved before implementation.

findings.finding: MC-19 solution pages may overlap MC-20-23.
findings.evidence: MC-20-22 own family pages; MC-23 owns bundle comparison and upgrade paths; MC-15 already proposes mareaSolutions and six bundle routes.
findings.impact: The page ownership boundary must be decided with the Master Prompt.

conclusion: The roadmap and handoff define the MC-19 objective and audiences but not a contractual, implementable scope. The required next artefact is a documented scope proposal and an explicit owner decision, not code. The baseline is verified and no MC-19 implementation exists.
